objectives: Build a communication plan covering who, what, why, how, when and owner
Choose suitable channels based on message complexity and sensitivity
Tailor messages to executives, managers, users and developers
Write concise status updates using BLUF and RAG

terminology.definition: A plan describing what will be communicated to which stakeholders, how, when and by whom.
The medium used to communicate, such as meetings, email, chat, demos or intranet.
A channel allowing two-way, nuanced communication, such as face-to-face conversation.
Bottom Line Up Front: stating the key point or decision at the start of a message.
Red, Amber, Green ratings used to summarise project health.
A senior group that oversees a project, makes key decisions and resolves escalations.
A period of extra support immediately after go-live.

exercises.question: Which channel would you choose for: (a) telling reception staff their roles will change, (b) sharing the release date with IT support, (c) a quick question to a developer, (d) a monthly progress update to 300 staff?
exercises.answer: (a) **Face-to-face briefing** with Q&A, followed by written FAQs (sensitive). (b) **Email** plus calendar invite and Confluence page (formal record). (c) **Chat** (quick). (d) **Intranet article or newsletter** (broad awareness).

exercises.question: Write a 3-line BLUF status update for a sponsor: testing found 12 defects, 2 critical; fixes will take one week; go-live can stay on date if UAT is shortened by 2 days.
exercises.answer: **Status: Amber.** Go-live date can hold if UAT is shortened by 2 days; decision needed by Thursday. Testing found 12 defects (2 critical); fixes will be complete within one week.

exercises.question: Name four things a communication plan should specify for each audience.
exercises.answer: Any four of: audience, purpose, key message/content, channel, frequency/timing, owner/sender, feedback mechanism.

quiz.question: For a sensitive message about job changes, the best channel is:
options: Face-to-face briefing followed by written detail
quiz.explanation: Rich, two-way channels suit sensitive messages; written follow-up provides a record.

quiz.question: BLUF means:
quiz.explanation: Lead with the main point or decision.

quiz.question: Executives usually most want:
options: Outcomes, cost, risk and decisions needed

quiz.question: An Amber RAG status typically means:
options: At risk but recoverable with action

quiz.question: Which is a communication mistake?
options: Announcing difficult news only by email
quiz.explanation: Difficult news needs a richer channel.

interview.question: How do you keep stakeholders informed?
interview.answer: With a communication plan based on stakeholder analysis: each group gets the information they need, in a suitable channel and frequency. Executives get concise BLUF updates, users get demos and plain-language guides, and the team gets daily conversation. I always include a way for people to give feedback.

interview.question: How would you communicate a delay to a sponsor?
interview.answer: Promptly and in person or by call, not just email. Lead with the impact and options: what's late, why, the effect on dates and benefits, recovery options with trade-offs, and my recommendation and the decision needed. Then confirm in writing and update the plan.

interview.question: How do you adapt your communication for technical and non-technical audiences?
interview.answer: For business audiences I focus on outcomes, impacts and examples in plain language and use visuals. For technical audiences I provide precise rules, data, edge cases and diagrams like sequence diagrams. I check understanding by asking people to explain back key points.

assignment.title: Communication plan
assignment.brief:
For a project of your choice (e.g. a school introducing a new parent communication app), create a communication plan for at least 6 audiences with purpose, content, channel, frequency, owner and feedback route.

Then write two messages about the same delay: one BLUF update for the sponsor and one plain-language note for end users.
